segments: Sultan Kaykaus.
Then envoys of the Mongols came,
demanding that Sultan 'Izz al-Din go to pay homage to the Khan.
He made excuses on account of the Greeks and Armenians who were his enemies,
[saying] that if he turned away,
they would seize his country from him.
Therefore, he sent Rukn al-Din, his middle brother,
and promised that at another time he too would go.
Concerning the accession of Guyuk his son.
At that time, when the Khan fell ill,
he sent envoys after Guyuk his son,
so that he might come and take over the kingdom,
in case the end should overtake him.
And when he set out to come and approached the vicinity,
the Khan departed from the world before Guyuk his son arrived at his presence {OCR?}.
Now the queen, the wife of the Khan,
who was the mother of Guyuk,
whose name was Töregene {Turkina},
was very wise and shrewd.
And on this account, Chagatai and the rest of the royal princes ordered
that she should administer the kingdom until they should all assemble together and make arrangements.
And when they had sent envoys to one another,
they all gathered in the days of spring.
From the east came Koten,
and Otchigin, the brother of Genghis
Khan,
and Alchidai (or Eljigidey?).
And from the west, Qara-Hülegü,
and Baidar,
and Yesu-Möngke {Turkan}, the sons of Chagatai.
And from the north, although Batu himself did not come in person,
he sent four of his brothers.
And from the Uighurs, the Emir Mas'ud Beg.
And from Khorasan, the Emir Arghun.
And from the country of the Romans (Rûm), Sultan Rukn al-Din.
And from Cilicia, King Hethum.
And from the Georgians (Iberians), David the Elder with David the Younger.
And from Syria, the brother of the Lord of Aleppo.
And from Baghdad, Fakhr al-Din, the Chief Judge (Qadi al-Qudat).
And envoys from the Franks.
And also envoys from 'Ala al-Din, the Lord of Alamut,
that is, the chief of the Ishmaelites (Assassins) who carry knives.
And although [the Khan?] had three sons who were fit for kingship:
Guyuk,
and Koten,
and Shiremun, a little child,
Queen Töregene, their mother, favored Guyuk,
and all the royal princes and nobles consented to her.
